questions.question_text: A square pyramid has apex $T$ and square base $ABCD$. $O$ is the centre of the base, $M$ is the midpoint of $AD$, and $TO$ is perpendicular to the base. What is the size of $\angle TOM$?

options.why: This assumes triangle $TOM$ is an isosceles right-angled triangle and gives an acute angle instead of the angle between the perpendicular height and the base.
This assumes triangle $TOM$ is equilateral, although $TO$ is perpendicular to $OM$.
This treats $T$, $O$ and $M$ as collinear, although $TO$ is perpendicular to $OM$.

questions.solution_text: $TO$ is perpendicular to the base and $OM$ lies in the base through $O$, so $\angle TOM=90^\circ$.

questions.question_text: A right triangular prism has triangular ends $ADE$ and $BCF$, with corresponding vertices $A$ and $B$, $D$ and $C$, and $E$ and $F$. The face $ADCB$ is a rectangle, and $CF$ is perpendicular to that face. What is the size of $\angle ACF$?

options.why: This confuses the $45^\circ$ angle between a square base's diagonal and an edge with the angle between $CA$ and $CF$.
This treats $CA$ and $CF$ as a straight line, although they are perpendicular.
This treats $CA$ and $CF$ as pointing in the same direction instead of being perpendicular.

questions.solution_text: $CA$ lies in the rectangular face $ADCB$ and passes through $C$. Since $CF$ is perpendicular to that face at $C$, $CA$ is perpendicular to $CF$, so $\angle ACF=90^\circ$.

questions.question_text: A square pyramid has apex $T$ and square base $ABCD$. $O$ is the centre of the base, and $TO$ is perpendicular to the base. What is the size of $\angle TOA$?

options.why: This uses the angle between a square's diagonal and a base edge instead of the angle between $TO$ and $OA$.
This assumes triangle $TOA$ is equilateral, although $TO$ is perpendicular to $OA$.
This treats $T$, $O$ and $A$ as collinear, although $TO$ is perpendicular to $OA$.

questions.solution_text: $TO$ is perpendicular to the base and $OA$ lies in the base through $O$, so $\angle TOA=90^\circ$.
